channel.title: Humanoid Robots News
channel.description: Daily high-signal humanoid robot news: launches, deployments, funding, notable demos and robot foundation models. One item per story.

item.title: Agility Robotics goes public as first U.S. specialist humanoid maker
item.description:
Agility Robotics has become the first publicly listed humanoid robotics company in the U.S., trading on Nasdaq as AGLT after completing its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI. The deal raised about $465 million before expenses to accelerate commercialization of its Digit humanoid.

Analysts call Agility the most commercially mature U.S. humanoid maker, with live warehouse deployments - Gartner research cited by TechTarget puts about 100 Digit robots at work today. The challenge now is proving repeatable, commercially viable operations at scale.

item.title: GXO and Apptronik sign LOI to deploy up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids over four years
item.description:
GXO Logistics signed a letter of intent with Apptronik to expand live trials of the Apollo humanoid in warehouses, with a path to a global rollout of up to 1,000 robots over four years. Trials starting in 2027 will test picking, packing, case and tote movement and sortation.

The rollout is conditional on the robots meeting agreed productivity, safety and operational targets, with first commercial deployment in North America targeted for late 2027 under a Robotics-as-a-Service model. The pair have worked together since 2024 and already ran a successful U.S. picking pilot.

item.title: GENTO unveils a 21-DoF dexterous hand at CoRL 2026 as its Marvin Pro powers NVIDIA's GR00T 2 demos
item.description:
GENTO, a humanoid brand incubated by Tianji Intelligence, showed its first 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand prototype at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026) in Austin, alongside its Luna humanoid and the TIANJI Marvin Pro dual-arm platform.

The hand uses a single linkage architecture aimed at four long-standing problems — backlash, fragility, backdrivability and fingertip force — while the Marvin Pro, running on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, demonstrated voice-command grasping.

NVIDIA also used a Marvin Pro to demo its new GR00T 2 world action model, including transferring human hand skills to the robot for two-handed tasks like preparing banana yogurt.

item.title: NeodraDynamics unveils Neo1, a 4-metre hydraulic humanoid for dangerous industrial jobs
item.description:
NeodraDynamics Robotics and JD Industrial unveiled Neo1, a four-metre-class heavy-duty hydraulic humanoid, at the 2026 China International Industry Fair (CIIF). It is built for “4D” jobs: dangerous, dirty, difficult and dull.

Unlike most humanoids, Neo1 uses a hybrid hydraulic-electric drive, with 41 active degrees of freedom and 39 joints on miniature digital hydraulic actuators. The company claims a 500 kg dual-arm payload and ±0.005 mm repeat positioning accuracy — company figures, not independently verified.

The robot is aimed at mining, disaster zones, nuclear facilities and deep-sea work, with JD Industrial helping match it to pilot projects.

item.title: Xinhua and UBTECH unveil Xinyan and Xinyu, billed as the first bionic humanoid news anchors
item.description:
Xinhua News Agency and UBTECH unveiled Xinyan and Xinyu, described as the world's first bionic humanoid robot news anchors, at a forum during the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing on Nov 5; the announcement was released Nov 11.

The human-scale anchors, visually designed with director Zhang Yimou, are built to deliver on-site news broadcasts, powered by Xinhua's “Xinhua Yudian” newsbot and UBTECH's biomimetic skin, embodied-AI hardware and emotion-driven language models.

Xinhua says the anchors will assist journalists with news presentation, multilingual delivery and on-site interaction — not replace them — with future uses planned in education, public venues and cultural exchange.

item.title: Matrix Robotics' MATRIX-3 debuts at CIIE as an autonomous humanoid tour guide
item.description:
Matrix Robotics' third-generation general-purpose humanoid, MATRIX-3, debuted at the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai, working as an autonomous tour guide in a crowded, noisy hall — its first real-world service deployment.

The 1.70 m, 65 kg robot runs the company's WAVE physical world base model, a “brain-cerebellum” system: WAVE handles perception, dialogue and planning while a motion-control model drives walking and gestures. It carries a 27-DoF rope-driven dexterous hand with 0.1 N fingertip sensing.

The tour system works without pre-set scripts, retrieving explanations based on visitor status — a company claim, with no independent test yet.

item.title: Humanoid shipments topped 22,000 in H1 2026, up nearly 300% year on year, Counterpoint says
item.description:
Over 22,000 humanoid robots shipped globally in the first half of 2026, up nearly 300% year on year, according to Counterpoint Research, with shipments expected to top 50,000 by year-end. Unitree leads with 31% share.

The figures came with the announcement of GITEX World RobotiX in Dubai (Dec 8-11), where Unitree, UBTECH, Chery's AiMOGA and others will show new humanoids and embodied-AI systems.

Why it matters: the clearest market-wide yardstick yet for 2026 — shipments are scaling fast and Chinese makers dominate volume, though most deployments remain pilots. Intelligent CIO

item.title: UBTECH partners with China Telecom's Tianyi to push humanoids into homes, targeting 100,000 units in three years
item.description:
UBTECH and Tianyi Telecom Terminal, a China Telecom subsidiary, signed a deal on Nov 9 aiming to help the home-companion robot market pass 1 million units and the humanoid terminal market pass 100,000 units within three years.

The partners will sell through telecom stores, offer robot rentals and service bundles, and run hands-on trials in shops, plus a joint lab on product validation and standards.

Why it matters: a major carrier's retail network is now aimed at getting humanoids into homes — though the 1M and 100K figures are industry targets, not UBTECH's own deliveries. Unite.AI

item.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5; Apptronik Apollo 2 humanoids hit 96% kitting car parts on Mercedes-Benz lines
item.description:
Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2.5, its newest vision-language-action model, and paired the launch with a factory proof of concept: Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid, fitted with a five-finger SharpaWave hand, sorted metal brackets from bulk bins into vehicle-specific sequencing trays on active Mercedes-Benz production lines in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany.

  • 96% success on the kitting task, per DeepMind. The company did not say how many robots ran, how many attempts were counted, or for how long.
  • Gemini Robotics ER tracked the job while Gemini Robotics 2.5 drove the arms and hands.
  • Across more than 200 evaluated tasks (tying bows, serving with tongs, pipetting), DeepMind reports 30% to 100% higher success and 20% to 30% faster completion than the previous version. These are company figures with no independent evaluation yet.
  • DeepMind says Gemini 4 Argon accelerated development, including generating simulated practice runs, and it open-sourced an ASIMOV-Jailbreak robot safety benchmark.
  • Access is rolling out to robotics partners only, with no public download or API.

Sources: Google DeepMind blog, DeepMind on X, Unite.AI.

item.title: China's UniX AI raises RMB 500M (~$70M) Pre-A for service humanoids, with customer Greenland Group joining as investor
item.description:
Suzhou-based UniX AI, which makes the Wanda and Panther wheeled dual-arm humanoids and the Martian biped, closed a RMB 500 million Pre-A round, eight months after a RMB 300 million raise. Existing backers Xienuo and Yonghua added again; new investors include property developer Greenland Group, sensor maker Keli Sensing and Huagong Venture Capital.

  • Greenland is already a customer and joins as a strategic investor, with plans to deploy robots in building security, hotels and elder care.
  • The company claims more than 100 deliveries a month since late 2025, with a peak above 300, and deployments at Hilton and other hotel chains. These figures are company claims.
  • No valuation was disclosed.

Sources: Spectrum, EastFrontier, Zhidx (Chinese).

item.title: LG Electronics targets late-2027 sales of its Nvidia-built bipedal humanoid, starting with research labs, and opens a Silicon Valley robotics hub
item.description:
At a Robotics Investor Forum on Nov 9, LG Electronics laid out its humanoid roadmap with Nvidia: unveil the bipedal robot in the first quarter of 2027 (Korean press expects CES 2027) and commercialize it in the second half of 2027, selling first to universities and research institutes along with developer tools.

  • LG builds the hardware, including its AXIUM actuators, while Nvidia supplies the software stack. AXIUM is slated for outside sales next year.
  • Its wheeled CLOiD robot is being validated at LG's Tennessee washing-machine plant, trained with Nvidia's Isaac GR00T to hang 4 kg top panels, and in Changwon.
  • LG has 170,000 hours of robot training data and aims for over 500,000 hours by year end.
  • Korean press reports a new North American robotics research base in Santa Clara opening this month, and current humanoid capacity of only a few hundred units a year (an industry estimate).

Sources: Financial News, Maeil Business, Herald Business.

item.title: Nvidia unveils GR00T 2, an open world action model for humanoids, with an onboard Turbo version running on Unitree G1
item.description:
At the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin on Monday, Nov 9, Nvidia introduced GR00T 2, an open "world action model" built on Cosmos that predicts future video and robot actions together. It runs on parallel grippers, dexterous hands and humanoids, and launched alongside Isaac Lab 3.0.

  • Trained on robot data plus 100,000 hours of human first-person video that Nvidia is releasing openly.
  • Nvidia says it completed 40 of 50 evaluated tasks at least once with no task-specific demos, averaging 71% success with one demonstration and 95% with five (company figures; The Next Web notes the tasks were ones the model could already learn well).
  • GR00T 2 Turbo, a 2B-parameter version, runs onboard a Unitree G1's Jetson Thor at 124 ms per prediction, steering whole-body tasks like serving popcorn and clearing tables, per the research page.
  • Foxconn, Siemens and Nexuni are testing it; none has announced production use yet.

More: The Robot Report.

item.title: Boston Dynamics puts scooter wheels on Atlas to stress-test its learned whole-body controller
item.description:
Boston Dynamics released a video on Nov 9 of its electric Atlas humanoid rolling through a mock warehouse with off-the-shelf scooter rims bolted to its ankle motors, pulling off jumps, 360-degree spins and quick side dashes (The Verge).

  • The company calls wheeled Atlas "a research testbed," not a product. The point was to see how faithfully a reinforcement-learning whole-body controller works with real actuators running at their limits under sustained high torque.
  • One custom adapter was the only new hardware; in software each wheel is modeled as an ankle that can spin continuously, according to controls engineer Andy Wu.
  • Boston Dynamics' post on X passed 2,000 likes and 129,000 views within hours.

More: The Robot Report.

item.title: Industrial-equipment maker Topstar unveils Star, a full-size bipedal humanoid for factory sorting and material handling
item.description:
Dongguan-based Topstar, which already sells injection-molding machines and CNC tools, showed Star, its first bipedal humanoid, at its TOPS DAY event on Nov 7 (Interesting Engineering via Yahoo Tech).

  • Star is 172 cm tall, weighs 72 kg, has seven-axis arms and a 10 kg dual-arm payload, and is aimed at small-batch sorting, multi-step tasks and material handling.
  • Topstar says it ran more than 30 scenario validations over the past year, but it disclosed no pricing, availability, battery life or customer deployments, so real-factory performance is unproven.
  • Its machine-tool subsidiary also launched the S400 five-axis machine for making humanoid parts such as joints and housings.

item.title: PrimeBOT says its 10,000th personal robot rolled off the line, doubling output in two weeks
item.description:
Chinese robotics company PrimeBOT said on Sunday, Nov 8, that its 10,000th personal robot has come off the production line, just 14 days after it announced the 5,000th unit on Oct 25. The figures come from a company statement to the Global Times and have not been independently verified.

  • PrimeBOT began handing over its first Q1 and T1 personal robots on Oct 1 in seven Chinese cities, including Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hangzhou.
  • Both models reportedly start at 19,999 yuan, about $3,000.
  • The same report cites market researcher SAG saying Chinese makers took more than 97% of global humanoid shipments in the first half of 2026, with AgiBot (about 8,400 units) passing Unitree (about 5,900) for the first time.

Why it matters: it is one of the fastest consumer embodied-AI production ramps reported so far, though the company hasn't said how many units have actually been delivered to customers.

item.title: Tau Robotics' teleoperated humanoid house cleaners go viral as it adds weekly subscriptions at $60 a visit
item.description:
Videos of Tau Robotics' humanoid "Sergey" scrubbing a toilet in a San Francisco home were among the most-shared robot clips on X this weekend. The San Francisco startup runs an invite-only home-cleaning service using modified Unitree G1 humanoids, and it has now moved past its $30-per-robot-hour pilot pricing.

  • Tau's service terms now list $50 per humanoid per hour, with two robots normally sent, so a one-hour visit is $100.
  • Recurring plans are cheaper: The Gadgeteer reports $60 a visit weekly, $80 every two weeks and $90 every four weeks.
  • The robots are not autonomous. A trained operator drives each one remotely through head and wrist cameras, and every visit is recorded to train future autonomous models.

An MIT Technology Review reporter who booked a visit found the robots thorough but slow, and a customer review said two robots finished about 80% of one floor in an hour before batteries needed swapping.

item.title: ATI Robotics' Sherpa Mecha factory humanoid cleared for continued U.S. sale after national-security review
item.description:
ATI Robotics says five of its platforms, including the Sherpa Mecha factory humanoid, the Sherpa 10K tugger and the Sherpa FlexFork, have been cleared from the FCC Covered List, the list that blocks foreign-built connected robots from new U.S. sales, under a notice dated Oct 30. The company announced it in a press release on Nov 6.

  • ATI says Sherpa Mecha is one of only two humanoids cleared so far and the only one built for factory work, so it can keep selling and servicing robots in the U.S. while most imported rivals can't.
  • That "one of only two" claim and its deployment figures are company-reported, as the Servo briefing notes.

Why it matters: U.S. security rules are quickly becoming a market filter for humanoids, and clearance is now a selling point on its own.

item.title: Figure's San Jose HQ fills with dozens of walking Figure 03 robots in new campus videos
item.description:
Figure founder Brett Adcock posted two roughly 90-second campus walkthroughs on Nov 6 and Nov 7 showing dozens of Figure 03 humanoids walking and standing around the company's San Jose headquarters — on the lawn, along outdoor paths, in the lobby beside employees with coffee, and on wireless charging pads by the entrance.

  • The Nov 6 clip, captioned "One day the entire world will look like this," had drawn more than 5,000 likes and about 387,000 views by this evening. A second clip on Nov 7, captioned "F.03 humanoid robots," covers the same ground in the opposite direction.
  • Adcock said in the spring that Figure had about 500 employees and wanted more humanoids than people walking the halls. Humanoids Daily says the new videos suggest that goal is close, if it has not already been met.
  • Figure marked its 1,000th Figure 03 in July and said in April that BotQ had reached one robot per hour. It has not published a production total since July, and Adcock did not say how many robots were on campus in the videos.
  • Almost none of the robots in the clips are doing a task beyond walking or standing. Figure has named a few customer sites, including BMW's Spartanburg plant and Catalyst Brands in Reno, but has not said how many robots are doing paid work.

These videos are a fleet-scale campus demo, not a new customer deployment. Sources: Humanoids Daily; Adcock's Nov 6 post on X; his Nov 7 follow-up.

item.title: Atlas battery pack to use 70 Samsung SDI 2170 cells totaling about 1.3 kWh, report says
item.description:
Unconfirmed industry report. The Elec, citing industry sources on Nov 6, says Hyundai Motor has finalized battery specs for Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid: each robot will use 70 cylindrical Samsung SDI 2170 cells (21 mm by 70 mm, 5,000 mAh each), for a pack of about 1.3 kWh.

  • LG Energy Solution has also been selected as a supplier, but Samsung SDI is expected to handle most of the initial volume while production remains small.
  • A capacity figure is not a runtime. How long Atlas can work still depends on the task, payload, motion and onboard compute. The Elec cites a typical humanoid operating window of about two to four hours; that has not been demonstrated publicly for this pack.
  • Boston Dynamics has previously said Atlas can navigate to a charging station, swap its own batteries and return to work.
  • The report repeats that Atlas mass production is scheduled for 2028 or later. Neither Boston Dynamics nor Samsung SDI has confirmed the cell count or pack size.

The Oct 28 coverage that Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution were in the Atlas battery lineup still stands; this is the first published pack specification. Also: Humanoids Daily.

item.title: Inside Unitree's Hangzhou factory, robots are still mostly built by hand, visitor notes and filings show
item.description:
Investor Josef Chen toured Unitree's Hangzhou factory and found that most robots are still put together by hand. In the actuator building he saw "one or two new automated lines"; the rest of the floor was people running winding machines. Visitors were not allowed to take photos inside.

  • Unitree's filings put all of its machinery at about $1.7 million on the books at the end of 2025. The company made almost 32,000 robots that year (about 26,000 of them quadrupeds), or roughly $50 of machinery per robot.
  • Direct labour was 8.1% of 2025 cost of goods, versus 81.7% materials. Chen estimates labour would be about 40% of costs at US wages.
  • A February Unitree video of G1 humanoids assembling parts in its own factory, billed as "an actual deployment," passed 28 million views. The IPO prospectus is more cautious: it calls that work a pilot and says assembly is "currently mainly manual."
  • Three quarters of Unitree's humanoid revenue in the first nine months of 2025 came from research and education, and less than 5% from factories or other industrial customers. Chen notes that half or more of the "industry" category was robots giving guided tours.

Chen discloses investments in several US hardware firms, including Minerva, a US humanoid maker. Sources: Humanoids Daily; Chen's factory notes.

item.title: Musk says Tesla will probably rent Optimus robots, with build cost ~$30K falling toward $20K
item.description:
At the 33rd Annual Baron Investment Conference on Nov 6, Elon Musk said Tesla will probably rent Optimus humanoid robots rather than sell them outright, when asked whether the company would rent or sell the bots.

  • Build-cost estimate: about as much as a car at first (~$30,000), falling toward ~$20,000 over time — these are manufacturing costs, not rental prices.
  • No rental price, term length or customer eligibility has been announced.
  • External company deliveries remain targeted around late 2027; early Fremont production is already running on a line sized for up to 1 million units a year.
  • Musk also said a sufficiently capable humanoid should deliver at least five times a human's weekly productivity by working continuously (company target, not demonstrated at scale).

Label the rental preference as a conference remark with a hedge ("probably"), not a locked commercial program. Sources: Not a Tesla App; Baron conference coverage on X.

item.title: Swiss startup Embodied AI unveils AIR wheeled factory humanoid at Humanoid Europe, opens orders
item.description:
Lausanne-based Embodied AI (EPFL spinout) unveiled AIR on Nov 6 at Humanoid Europe 2026 in Munich: a wheeled, two-armed upper-body robot built to work beside factory staff without a safety cage. Orders open after the unveil.

  • Design: heavy components in the torso with light, tendon-driven compliant arms that yield on contact; investor notes cite a ~2 kg arm lifting ~5 kg (company has not published height, weight, full payload or price).
  • Deployment model: remote teleoperation from the first shift, with the company saying the robot takes over the task on its own within about a month using recorded shift data.
  • Company-reported claim (unconfirmed independently): ~95% average task success across paid pilots with unnamed consumer-electronics and automotive/industrial customers.
  • CE marking targeted for 2027 under the EU Machinery Regulation; no delivery schedule published.

Sources: Humanoids Daily; BusinessWire.

item.title: Agility Robotics begins trading on Nasdaq as AGLT, first U.S. pure-play public humanoid company
item.description:
Agility Robotics said its common stock and warrants began trading today on Nasdaq under AGLT and AGLTW, after completing its SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI on Nov 4. The company calls itself the first U.S. publicly listed pure-play humanoid robotics firm with active commercial deployments.

  • Business combination and related financings provided about $465 million in gross capital before expenses.
  • Agility cites more than 65,000 hours of Digit operation in real facilities and more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5 (subject to milestones and specs).
  • Independent coverage from The Robot Report said shares opened above the $10 SPAC reference price.

Source: Agility Robotics press release. Also: The Robot Report.

item.title: Apple researchers’ HALO system: Unitree G1 trained only in sim hits 91% on real-home skills (preprint claim)
item.description:
Apple-affiliated researchers posted Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation (arXiv:2611.06908) introducing HALO — Humanoid Autonomy, Learned in simulation, running Onboard — for a modified Unitree G1. Motion data came from about 300 hours of synthetic trajectories in 1,000 procedurally generated homes; the authors say there was no teleoperation training data.

  • Author-reported result (unconfirmed independently): 91% success across 360 single-skill real-world trials in six unmapped environments (sit, go-to-object, door sidestep, crouch/crawl, push box).
  • Chained multi-step tasks scored lower (about 70% average on three sequences in one real room).
  • Hardware runs untethered with a head camera and rear Mac mini; code for data generation, training and deployment is public.

Source: Humanoids Daily. Paper: arXiv:2611.06908. Project: Apple ML HALO page.

item.title: Unitree CEO says GPT-6-powered humanoids can paint and play chess with zero task training (CIIE remarks)
item.description:
At China’s Import Expo in Shanghai on Nov 5, Unitree founder Wang Xingxing said the company’s humanoids, powered by OpenAI’s GPT-6, can paint and play chess without prior task-specific training, including steps like changing brush water and blending pigments from live model inference.

  • Unconfirmed company claim: remarks come from the CEO at a trade fair, not from a published benchmark or independent scorecard; no attempt counts or success rates were reported by SCMP.
  • Wang framed the remaining industry bottleneck as a “last-millimetre” mechanical gap rather than digital planning.
  • Separate coverage notes Unitree’s public skill demos still rely on calibrated motion tooling and (for chess) a specialist engine, so “zero training” should be read carefully.

Source: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Speedbot unveils Weldroid-W1 bipedal humanoid welder, aims for shipyard trials this year
item.description:
Changsha-based Speedbot unveiled the Weldroid-W1 on Nov 4, a full-size two-legged humanoid aimed at welding work, and said it plans shipyard welding trials before year-end.

  • Listed specs: about 170 cm / 60 kg, 27 degrees of freedom, 10 kg arm payload and 30 kg whole-body payload.
  • Sensing stack includes stereo cameras and LiDAR in the head plus a handheld 3D structured-light scanner; the company says an onboard AI brain handles motion and navigation.
  • Weld speed, inspection pass rates, runtime and price were not published with the unveil.

Source: ServoSpace.

item.title: RoboColosseum opens 100+ real robots for free AI testing, and no policy finished a single Unitree G1 humanoid task in 625 trials
item.description:
RoboColosseum, an open evaluation initiative from Hugging Face, BitRobot, the Singapore Embodied AI Centre and researcher Jiafei Duan, launched with more than 100 physical robots, over 140 real-world scenes and 10,000 free evaluation hours for academic teams. Unitree backs it, and its G1 is the platform for the humanoid category.

  • In the first humanoid results, none of five vision-language-action policies fully completed any of five G1 tasks (carrying a box, folding a towel, loading a washing machine), even after fine-tuning on 100 demonstrations per task.
  • Partial-progress scores ranged from 13.3% to 23.2% across 625 logged trials.
  • Rollout videos of successes and failures are being shared openly on the Hugging Face Hub.

Source: Humanoids Daily. Launch thread: @RoboColosseum on X; Unitree's note: @UnitreeRobotics.

item.title: JD.com launches a "Physical AI Acceleration Plan" focused on embodied robots, plans 10M hours of human video data in two years
item.description:
At the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen on Nov. 4, JD.com technology committee chairman Cao Peng announced the "JD Physical AI Acceleration Plan," whose first phase centers on embodied-intelligence robots, with investment across data, bases, manufacturing, sales, logistics and service.

  • JD is building an embodied-AI data collection center and aims to gather more than 10 million hours of real-world human video and over 1 million hours of robot operation data within two years. It says it has already collected over 100,000 real tasks across 100+ scenarios.
  • AGIBOT humanoids are already working in JD Logistics' "Wolf" warehouse.
  • Cao repeated JD Logistics' target of buying 3 million robots, 1 million autonomous vehicles and 100,000 drones over five years (first announced in September).

Sources: AI123, IT Home via Sina (Chinese).

item.title: Tesla shows its latest gold Optimus beside the production Cybercab at China's Import Expo, opening Nov 5
item.description:
Tesla has its first dedicated zone at the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai (Nov. 5–10), part of the 2,700-square-meter Lingang showcase, the expo's largest single exhibit area. First-look photos posted Wednesday show Optimus humanoids standing next to the production Cybercab.

  • Organizers say the latest-generation gold Optimus robots will act out factory work, carry luggage and walk a dog.
  • The display is static: Tesla has no plans to sell the Cybercab or run robotaxi rides in China.
  • No new Optimus specs, pricing or reservation dates were announced; Elon Musk recently denied a report that Optimus reservations open in December.

Sources: CyberCab.News, Shanghai government.

item.title: Korea's KIST shows KAPEX, a humanoid with over 90% locally made core parts, as LG builds a supply chain around it
item.description:
South Korea's science ministry gave its November Korea Science and Technology Award to KIST's Lee Jong-won for KAPEX, a bipedal AI humanoid whose actuators, joints, sensors and control AI were built domestically, with more than 90% of core components made in Korea.

  • KAPEX walks while carrying more than 20 kg and uses fingertip slip sensors to adjust its grip, from paper cups to heavy boxes.
  • KIST transferred the core technology to LG Electronics. LG handles the platform, LG AI Research the physical AI, LG Energy Solution solid-state batteries, and Robostar mass production.
  • Field tests are expanding into homes and hospitals, though the team says long-duration autonomous work is still unsolved.

Source: Seoul Economic Daily.

item.title: Rainbow Robotics says it has sold nearly 200 RB-Y1 wheeled humanoids and plans RB-Y2 mass production by next summer
item.description:
At Robo World 2026, which opened Nov. 4 at KINTEX near Seoul with 402 companies, Samsung-owned Rainbow Robotics said it has sold nearly 200 of its RB-Y1 mobile humanoids worldwide.

  • The company aims to get safety certification for the next-generation RB-Y2 and start mass production by next summer.
  • Rainbow keeps its working humanoids on wheels for safety and plans to focus on manufacturing until about 2030, with pilots at Daedong, Samsung Medical Center and bakery chain Sungsimdang.
  • The show floor also featured Chinese Unitree G1 humanoids dancing and an RB-Y1 sorting flowers, which Rainbow admits still makes mistakes.

Source: Aju Press.

item.title: South Korea opens its first AI Humanoid Data Factory, with 12 teleoperated humanoids recording training data
item.description:
The state-funded Korea Institute of Machinery and Materials (KIMM) and ETRI opened the country's first facility built to mass-produce training data for two-legged humanoids on Tuesday. It runs 12 humanoids across about 1,000 square meters, with plans to grow to 25.

  • Researchers teleoperate the robots through tasks like pulling food from a fridge, handling laundry, tidying a sofa and working car controls; each motion trains vision-language-action models that go back onto the robots for testing.
  • It's part of the science ministry's K-Moonshot humanoid mission, alongside the 2.3 trillion won (about $1.7B) budgeted through 2030 for the humanoid industry.
  • The factory is due to open to outside companies, universities and institutes in stages from late 2027.

Source: Aju Press

item.title: Carnegie Mellon unveils Pixel, an under-$15,000 wheeled humanoid and full learning stack it plans to open-source
item.description:
CMU researchers Tony Tao and Jason Liu, advised by Ruslan Salakhutdinov and Deepak Pathak, released Pixel: a wheeled humanoid with a 17-DoF human-proportioned upper body, holonomic base and vertical lift that can be assembled for under $15,000.

  • It ships with sensorized human-worn grippers for collecting demos without a robot, VR and leader-arm teleoperation, a shared whole-body controller and one policy pipeline for human and robot data.
  • Policies trained from human demos reached 82.0% average task progress on three mobile-manipulation tasks, and 78.7% from robot teleop on three others.
  • The project page says the system will be "Open Sourced Soon"; no public repo yet.

Read the paper on arXiv or the project page.

item.title: Xiaomi says its humanoids worked an eight-hour shift sorting car parts at its EV factory
item.description:
Xiaomi showed its humanoids autonomously sorting center-console side covers at its car factory for more than eight hours, with two charging breaks, and says they met the station's daily production needs.

Xiaomi says the robots detect and recover from errors on their own and coordinate with line systems. It hasn't disclosed throughput, error rates or how often humans stepped in, so treat the result as a company demo rather than an independent test.

Sources: Humanoids Daily and the video on X

item.title: Hyundai Mobis starts building prototype actuators for Boston Dynamics' Atlas this month, aiming for supply in 2028
item.description:
Hyundai Mobis is producing prototype actuators for Atlas at its Uiwang Research Center starting in November, and will validate performance and reliability with Boston Dynamics ahead of expected supply in 2028.

  • Mobis says it has a confirmed actuator order and is also developing hand grippers, perception modules and controllers to sell to other humanoid makers.
  • It's creating a dedicated robotics-parts organization and roughly doubling staff for it.
  • Reports that Mobis will supply all 31 Atlas actuators and build a 350,000-unit US plant are from Korean press and not confirmed by the company.

Sources: The Robotics Media and The Asia Business Daily

item.title: Agility Robotics shareholders approve its SPAC merger; deal closes Nov 4 and AGLT starts trading on Nasdaq Nov 5
item.description:
Churchill Capital Corp XI shareholders approved the business combination with Agility Robotics, the maker of the Digit humanoid. The deal is expected to close on November 4, 2026, and the combined company should begin trading on Nasdaq as AGLT (warrants AGLTW) on November 5.

  • Expected gross capital is about $465M: roughly $164M from the trust account, about $201M from a $10/share PIPE led by Foxconn, and $100M already received.
  • Agility pitches itself as the only US-listed pure-play humanoid company with active commercial deployments, citing more than 65,000 hours of real-world Digit operation.
  • Separately, coverage notes a pipeline of more than 30 prospective customers and GXO adding Digit at two more US sites in early 2027.

Sources: Agility press release, Robotics & Automation News.

item.title: Brett Adcock shows newly built Figure 03 humanoids walking out of the BotQ factory and across Figure's campus on their own
item.description:
Figure CEO Brett Adcock posted a short clip on X of freshly manufactured Figure 03 robots leaving the BotQ factory and walking across the campus parking lot, past cars and people, toward another building. "Newly manufactured F.03 robots leaving BotQ and heading across campus," he wrote.

It is a demo of the fleet growing rather than a business update: the post gives no new production total or customer-delivery figures. Figure is also developing its next-generation Figure 04.

Sources: Humanoids Daily, CyberRobo on X.

item.title: AGIBOT livestreams six G2 robots running a convenience store for 24 hours straight
item.description:
AGIBOT's "Robots Never Clock Out" challenge puts six G2 wheeled humanoids through a full convenience-store shift on a public livestream, from 10:00 a.m. Nov 2 to 10:00 a.m. Nov 3 China time (6:00 p.m. Nov 1 to 6:00 p.m. Nov 2 PT).

  • Planned work covers the lunch and evening rushes, overnight duty and breakfast prep.
  • Tasks include stocking shelves, making coffee, preparing hot food, greeting customers and clearing rubbish.

Caveat: the event length doesn't prove each robot worked continuously or fully autonomously. AGIBOT hasn't published an intervention policy or success scoring.

Source: Humanoids Daily.

item.title: Nearly 90 robot teams race up Mount Tai's 3,100 stone steps in China's first robot mountain-climbing challenge
item.description:
The CMG World Robot Mount Tai Challenge in Tai'an, Shandong, sent humanoid, quadruped and exoskeleton robots up a 3.9 km stretch of ancient trail with about 3,100 stone steps and 600 m of climb on November 2.

Legged robots dominated: according to X's news summary, a Unitree quadruped from Beijing Lingyi Technology won the legged speed race in 43 minutes 41 seconds, and robot dogs outpaced the humanoids. Some quadrupeds also carried supplies up the route.

Sources: Euronews, X news summary.

item.title: ID Logistics and Terra Robotics team up to put humanoids into German warehouses, with a live pilot planned within six months
item.description:
Contract logistics firm ID Logistics (450 sites worldwide, 17 in Germany) and Terra Robotics, a multi-brand integrator and Unitree distributor, formed a strategic partnership on November 1 to move humanoids from demos to real warehouse work.

  • Two Unitree G1 EDU6 robots, nicknamed IDA and Heinz, already sort cardboard boxes from shipping bags using five-fingered tactile hands.
  • The partners will pick one of four or five candidate tasks and run a live pilot at an ID Logistics site within six months, possibly with a UBTECH or Unitree robot.
  • No financial terms or pilot site were disclosed.

Sources: The Robotics Media, ID Logistics press release (German PDF).

item.title: DEEP Robotics humanoids join traffic police at the Hangzhou Marathon
item.description:
At the Hangzhou Marathon on November 1, Hangzhou-based DEEP Robotics and local traffic authorities put its Hangxing No. 2 traffic and security humanoids on duty at four points around Huanglong Sports Center, with human officers handling complex situations. The race had 36,000 runners.

  • Hangxing No. 2 is built on DEEP Robotics' 178 cm DR02 humanoid, rated IP66 and able to work from -20 to 55 C.
  • Its jobs: intersection monitoring, preset-route patrols, warnings about pedestrians crossing and vehicles cutting in, traffic gestures, safety announcements and answering public questions.
  • It carries a 275 TOPS computer with LiDAR, a depth camera and a wide-angle camera. Capability details are the company's own and not independently tested.

Sources: Global Times, RobotsBeat.

item.title: Foxconn says more than 10 humanoid robots are already working at its Texas sites, built on Nvidia GR00T
item.description:
Brand Cheng, chairman of Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII), told Reuters on October 30 that more than 10 humanoid robots are deployed for internal use at Foxconn's Texas facilities, where it builds AI servers for Nvidia, and that the rollout will extend beyond Texas.

  • The robots are wheeled, not legged. FII introduced two models in October: one that lifts things vertically and one that bends at the waist for assembly plus loading and unloading.
  • FII is building the robots' AI on Nvidia's Isaac GR00T foundation model.
  • Foxconn hasn't shared costs, specific tasks or a rollout timetable; the deployment count is the company's own figure.

Sources: CNA (Reuters), HumanoidBeat.

item.title: UK gets its first home insurance policy for domestic humanoid robots (Adrian Flux and Tokio Marine HCC)
item.description:
Broker Adrian Flux and underwriter Tokio Marine HCC International have launched what they call the UK's first household insurance policy for domestic humanoid robots, sold as part of Adrian Flux home cover. They say it appears to be the world's first policy that protects the home as well as the robot.

  • Covers accidental damage to and theft of the robot, sudden damage it causes to the home or belongings (up to £5,000), and personal liability if it injures someone or damages property.
  • Also pays for emergency recovery or safe disablement after a sudden malfunction.
  • Premiums are quoted case by case; eligible models and liability limits aren't published. The insurers expect domestic robots in UK homes from 2027.

Sources: Insurance Business, Tokio Marine HCC announcement, Insurance Times.

item.title: Meta reportedly built a humanoid prototype called Max with China's Fourier in three months, and Max 2 is underway (report)
item.description:
Unconfirmed, single-source report. According to The Information, Meta worked with Chinese humanoid maker Fourier to build a prototype humanoid, internally called Max, in roughly three months. Reuters said it could not immediately verify the report.

  • Max is about 1.5 m tall, weighs about 106 lb (48 kg), runs on Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip, and has a face display, speakers and five-fingered hands.
  • Meta's VP of product for robotics, Li-Chen Miller, reportedly spent almost two months at Fourier's Shanghai factory; Max was shown to employees at an internal robotics summit in late August.
  • A second version, Max 2, started in September with a redesigned torso, better hands, a projector and stair-navigation sensors.
  • Meta frames the robots as a physical body for its Muse AI agent doing household tasks, but told The Information the work is internal research with no plans to sell units.

Coverage: The Robotics Media, Investing.com, AI Weekly.

item.title: Lightberry's Lumi becomes the first humanoid cleared by the US Department of War and exempted from the FCC's foreign-robot ban
item.description:
San Francisco startup Lightberry says its Lumi interactive humanoids received a Conditional Approval from the US Department of War on October 30, and the FCC's Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau exempted them from its Covered List the same day (Public Notice DA 26-1181). Since July, new foreign-produced advanced robots on that list can't get the FCC authorization needed to be imported or sold in the US.

  • Lightberry is the only humanoid company among the newly exempted devices; the other robotics approvals went to warehouse and industrial platforms.
  • The approval rests on two commitments: Lightberry replaces Lumi's sensors, onboard computer and software with its own, and moves manufacturing to the US, starting with the body, head and hands.
  • It is conditional: breaking the onshoring plan or a false statement in the application can put Lumi back on the list. The plan's deadlines aren't public.
  • Per Robotica Guide, Lumi is built on a Unitree G1 base, and Founder Editions are priced at $39,990.

Sources: Lightberry announcement, HumanoidBeat.

item.title: Elon Musk says "No" to the report that Tesla will open Optimus reservations in December
item.description:
Follow-up to yesterday's item: after The San Francisco Standard reported, citing Humanoids Summit organizer Modar Alaoui, that Tesla would open Optimus reservations around the December 1 to 2 summit, Elon Musk replied "No" on X to a post asking whether Optimus ordering was coming in December.

Tesla hasn't announced any reservation window, price or delivery date. Musk's one-word reply addressed December ordering specifically, so it doesn't rule out a waitlist at some other time.

More: TSN, Tesla News Wire.

item.title: Agility Robotics now expects about $465M from its SPAC merger, below June's $620M target, with Nasdaq listing set for Nov 5
item.description:
Agility Robotics and Churchill Capital Corp XI said on Oct 30 that Agility expects to raise about $465 million through its SPAC merger. That is less than the roughly $620 million the company projected at a $2.5 billion valuation when the deal was announced in June.

  • About $164 million from Churchill XI's trust account
  • About $201 million from a PIPE at $10 per share, led by Foxconn
  • $100 million in equity funding already received after the deal was announced

Churchill XI shareholders vote on Nov 2. If approved, the deal is expected to close Nov 4 and the combined company would start trading on Nasdaq as AGLT on Nov 5, pitching itself as the first U.S.-listed pure-play humanoid maker with commercial deployments. Agility says it has more than $300 million in committed Digit 5 orders, with early-access deliveries in the first half of 2027.

Sources: The Robot Report and Agility's press release.

item.title: Tesla reportedly plans to open Optimus reservations in early December, timed to the Humanoids Summit (unconfirmed)
item.description:
The San Francisco Standard reports that Tesla is expected to open customer reservations for its Optimus humanoid in early December. The source is Modar Alaoui, organizer of the Humanoids Summit (Dec 1 to 2 in San Mateo), who says Tesla told him reservations would launch with his event or in the days after. Tesla has not confirmed this and didn't respond to the paper.

  • Tesla is a key summit partner and plans to demo Optimus V3 there.
  • The expected price is $20,000-plus; any deposit amount is unknown.
  • Robots likely won't ship for about a year. Musk said on the October earnings call that deliveries to outside companies should start around the end of 2027, after Fremont production began.

Source: The San Francisco Standard.

item.title: Beijing startup SynDexy delivers its first small batch of C1 humanoids for precision electronics assembly
item.description:
SynDexy, a Beijing humanoid startup, has delivered its first small batch of C1 humanoid robots built for precision assembly in electronics manufacturing, about six months after development started.

The company says the C1 hit over 98% success in key task tests. It plans to refine the robot and expand deployments in electronics plants but gave no further timeline. The figures are company-reported.

Source: RobotToday, citing PanDaily.

item.title: AGIBOT unveils AHA3 humanoid platform and GO-3 Preview model, proposes "Worken" metric for real robot work
item.description:
At its Innovation Day in Shanghai on Oct 29, AGIBOT rolled out a full humanoid stack and pitched a new way to measure whether robots actually do useful work, per its press release and announcement on X.

  • AHA3: its third-generation humanoid hardware architecture, combining locomotion, interaction and task-execution compute, Wi-Fi 6 and 5G, liquid-cooled joints and IP67-rated joints, plus a new OmniHand 3 family of dexterous hands.
  • GO-3 Preview: its next embodied foundation model combining reasoning, prediction and action, alongside the WITA-Omni 1.0 interaction model.
  • Link-U OS 1.0: a robot operating system now in partner trials, which AGIBOT says it will fully open-source by the end of 2026 and donate to the OpenAtom Foundation.
  • Worken: a proposed metric multiplying active robots by autonomous working hours by an output-efficiency ratio against a human benchmark, meant to replace "units shipped" as the yardstick.

The G2 Max industrial robot was also formally launched (it was first shown last week). More detail from Humanoids Daily and Korthos.

item.title: Paris startup Bleu Robotics raises a €5M pre-seed to teach factory humanoids new tasks from about ten demonstrations
item.description:
Bleu Robotics, founded in Paris by former Renault assembly-line manager Benoît Berkoukchi and INRIA research directors Jean-Baptiste Mouret and Serena Ivaldi, raised a €5 million pre-seed round co-led by Contrarian Ventures and OVNI Capital, with Kvanted, WEPA Ventures, Motier Ventures and Meta board member Charlie Songhurst, per EU-Startups and the company announcement.

  • Instead of a data-hungry end-to-end model, its "abductive learning" software infers the goal and constraints behind an operator's demonstration, learning a task from as few as ten demos.
  • Operators teach at the workstation with handheld gripper devices, no coding; the software is meant to run on any humanoid platform.
  • The company claims 99%+ accuracy on production-line tasks and targets a full humanoid deployment in under an hour (company claims, not independently verified).

Initial deployments are underway with automotive manufacturers and paper maker WEPA. Sifted has more on the approach.

item.title: Rokae delivers its 10,000th humanoid force-controlled arm; five Helios wheeled humanoids work at Schaeffler's Taicang plant
item.description:
Chinese robot maker Rokae says its 10,000th humanoid force-controlled arm came off its Shandong line in September, with more than 80 industrial partners using the arms in production, per The AI Insider.

  • The count covers only its humanoid arms, not its industrial or collaborative robots.
  • Five Rokae Helios wheeled humanoids fitted with AR Series arms are handling parts, assembly and inspection on a humanoid-component assembly line at Schaeffler's lighthouse factory in Taicang.
  • Each AR arm has seven force-controlled joints, and Rokae's MAC controller can run single-arm, dual-arm or 20-plus-joint humanoid setups.

It's a sign of the component supply chain behind humanoids scaling quickly in China.

item.title: Trump's Section 232 proclamation calls robot and machinery imports a security threat, citing humanoids, but imposes no tariffs yet
item.description:
President Trump signed a proclamation on Oct 28 agreeing with Commerce that imports of robotics, industrial machinery and their parts "threaten to impair the national security of the United States." The text specifically names humanoid and quadruped robots among the advanced robots that support the military.

  • No tariff yet: there's no duty rate, product list or effective date. Commerce and the U.S. Trade Representative are told to negotiate agreements with trading partners instead (fact sheet).
  • Timeline: a progress report is due in 180 days, and tariffs or other measures remain possible if talks fail, as Bloomberg Law notes.

For humanoid makers that rely on Chinese actuators and components, nothing changes at the border today, but the threat of future duties is now formally on the record.

item.title: Boston Dynamics reportedly lines up an all-Korean Atlas supply chain and tells suppliers to prepare parts for 10,000 humanoids
item.description:
Boston Dynamics has finalized its supplier lineup for the Atlas humanoid and asked the selected companies to get ready for purchase orders covering 10,000 units, KED Global reported on Oct 27, citing industry sources. This is a report, not confirmed by Boston Dynamics, and it describes a request to prepare, not a placed order.

  • Actuators and grippers: Hyundai Mobis, with actuators said to make up most of the robot's parts cost.
  • Batteries: Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution; cameras from a Mobis-led group with Namuga and IL, plus MCNEX and Cammsys for hand cameras.
  • Other parts: BH EVS for charging and CTR for control arms; the only non-Korean component is NVIDIA's processor.

Final quantities and prices aren't set, and first orders are expected around late 2027 or early 2028. Early Atlas units are slated for Hyundai's own Metaplant in Georgia. Machine Economy's breakdown stresses that the 10,000 figure is a planning number, not a shipment or contract.

item.title: Unitree's first earnings since its IPO: Q3 revenue up 70% to 665M yuan, but net profit falls 17% as R&D spending jumps
item.description:
Unitree Robotics reported its first quarterly results since its August listing in Shanghai, per the South China Morning Post and the company's Q3 filing.

  • Q3 revenue rose 69.93% year on year to 665 million yuan (about $100 million).
  • Net profit fell 17.37% to 112.7 million yuan, well below the roughly 224 million yuan analysts expected, according to Reuters.
  • Quarterly R&D spending jumped about 250% to 127 million yuan, around 19% of revenue, as Unitree invests in robot AI.
  • For the first nine months, revenue grew 55.7% to 1.82 billion yuan.

It's an early market test for China's best-known humanoid maker amid a tech-sector selloff.

item.title: XPeng's dedicated solid-state battery for the IRON humanoid enters small-batch production ahead of robot mass production
item.description:
XPeng vice president Gu Jie said at the Society of Automotive Engineers of China annual conference on Oct 28 that solid-state batteries built for the IRON humanoid have started rolling off the line in small batches, CnEVPost reports. IRON itself is still before start of production, with mass production planned by the end of 2026 and commercial deployment in stores from 2027.

  • The pack uses a high-energy-density design for the robot's tight internal space and is built to stop thermal runaway from spreading; it passes impact and nail-penetration tests.
  • Gu reportedly said it's about 30% lighter with about 30% more capacity than the previous pack (per a post on X).
  • Unclear: XPeng didn't say whether this is the all-solid-state chemistry it promised in 2025; a September report said the production IRON would use semi-solid-state cells instead. No volume or energy-density figures were given.

item.title: Westlake Robotics shows an upgraded WR1 model running humanoids through multi-room household chores without resets
item.description:
Hangzhou start-up Westlake Robotics, spun out of Westlake University, released videos of an improved version of its WR1 AI model, Vuntum reports.

  • A humanoid takes trousers and a T-shirt off a rack, then folds the trousers together with a second humanoid.
  • In a second run across kitchen, living room and bedroom, it moves corn from the fridge to an air-fryer basket, kneels to pick up toys, and straightens a duvet.

The company says the tasks run in sequence with no human resets or step-by-step prompting. These are company-made demo videos, and the cooking stops at the fryer basket.

item.title: Reward AI shows its glove-trained OM-1 model driving humanoids on last-mile delivery and stairs
item.description:
Robotics startup Reward AI, whose team previously built DexCap, HumanPlus and ALOHA, posted new videos of its OM-1 robot model running humanoids indoors and outdoors: unloading Amazon, Walmart and DHL packages from a Cybertruck bed for last-mile delivery, and picking things up while standing on stairs.

OM-1 is trained only on data from people wearing Reward AI's 7-degree-of-freedom Omnibody Hand glove, with no teleoperation and no on-robot data, and the company says one policy runs across arms and humanoids. The post drew about 430 likes and 64,000 views within hours.

  • These are company-run stress tests, not a commercial rollout.
  • No weights, code or API have been released.

Sources: Reward AI on X, Reward AI OM-1 blog post.

item.title: Shanghai's International Embodied Intelligence Competition puts about 1,000 humanoid robots through real-world tasks
item.description:
The International Embodied Intelligence Competition wrapped up in Shanghai on Sunday, with about 1,000 humanoid robots from more than 800 teams competing across 23 categories spanning industrial production, services, special operations and everyday life.

The event was the centerpiece of the 2026 Global Developer Pioneers Summit, which drew more than 300 robot hardware companies and over 200 supply-chain firms. A Pudong official said more than 30 humanoid models have launched in the district, calling it the world's densest cluster of mass-produced humanoids (an official claim, not independently verified).

Source: China Daily.

item.title: AgiBot launches Genie G2 Max, a heavy-payload wheeled humanoid lifting up to 50 kg, already in JD Logistics warehouses
item.description:
AgiBot released the Genie G2 Max, a safety-rated dual-arm embodied robot for depalletizing, palletizing, material transfer and production-line feeding. It is the third launch in AgiBot's "AI WAVE" release week.

  • Payload of 20 kg per arm, 40 kg rated with both arms and 50 kg peak, with arm repeatability within 0.5 mm.
  • A waist pitch joint lets it lean forward, so pallets can sit against a wall without a walkway behind them.
  • Hot-swappable dual batteries and self-charging for round-the-clock work.

AgiBot says the robot already depalletizes 80 cases and palletizes 75 cases an hour at a JD Logistics warehouse with over 99% success, and feeds parts on its own humanoid production line. Those figures are the company's own, and no price was given. The robot will be shown at AgiBot Innovation Day on Oct 29.

Source: Robrief.
